newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivorian leader says no plan to sack prime minister.
newsitem.headline: Ivorian leader says no plan to sack prime minister.

text.p: Ivory Coast President Henri Konan Bedie has dismissed speculation that he plans to sack Prime Minister Daniel Kablan Duncan, the spearhead of the country's ambitious privatisation and investment drive.
Speaking at a lunch with lawmakers on Thursday, Bedie recalled he had previously given a glowing account of the economy under Duncan, who forecasts 1996 growth at 7.0 percent.
"In view of this account, why think I would change prime minister? I am satisfied, and you also, of the prime minister and the performance of the government," Bedie said.
The government daily Fraternite-Matin, echoing Bedie's public endorsement, lauded economic achievements under Duncan.

Duncan steered the economy to a rebound after a 50 percent devaluation of the regional CFA franc currency in January 1994. Ivory Coast has fared much better than other French-speaking West African countries forced to devalue after pressure from France and Western donor institutions.

"One does not change a winning team, less still its captain," commented Fraternite-Matin. "The achievements of the government are appreciable. Devaluation has been a success. The economy is out of its low ebb."

Yet opposition newspapers pursued their speculation on the fate of Duncan, a 53-year-old technocrat appointed by Bedie in December 1993 when the president came to power after veteran head of state Felix Houphouet-Boigny died.

La Voie, mouthpiece of the Ivorian Popular Front party, reported on Friday that Bedie had removed the respected DCGTX department responsible for major government construction projects from control of the prime minister.
"It's Mr Duncan who is the target," a columnist wrote.
